stories.headline: BRICS Summit gets underway in Delhi as leaders meet and traffic is rerouted

agreed_facts.text: The BRICS Summit 2026 is currently underway in New Delhi.
Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in New Delhi for the summit.
PM Modi proposed a 10-point agenda for global governance.
Delhi Police issued traffic advisories for the duration of the summit.

contested.point: The primary focus of the summit

positions.claim: Russia advocates for BRICS to counter Western influence.
PM Modi emphasises strengthening BRICS identity and the global governance agenda.

contested.point: Bilateral meetings versus the overall BRICS agenda

positions.claim: Bilateral meetings on trade, energy and defence are the key components of the summit.
The summit's focus is collective proposals for global governance, not side deals.

framing.note: Led with PM Modi's proposals for strengthening BRICS and global governance.
Focused on local impact — Delhi's traffic advisories from VVIP movements.
Highlighted Russia's call for BRICS to counter the West and stronger bilateral ties.

jargon.plain: A Very Very Important Person — usually a head of state, whose movement gets roads closed and extra security.
The ways countries and international bodies jointly manage shared problems like trade, climate and security.
About how geography and politics interact — who has leverage over whom, and where.

people.name: Narendra Modi
people.who: Prime Minister of India, hosting the BRICS Summit.

people.name: Xi Jinping
people.who: President of the People's Republic of China, attending the summit.

people.name: Vladimir Putin
people.who: President of Russia, attending the summit and making geopolitical statements.

stories.headline: Saudi pipeline shut after drone attack as Houthis advance and Red Sea tension rises

agreed_facts.text: Saudi Arabia has shut down its East-West oil pipeline.
The pipeline shutdown followed a reported drone attack on pumping stations.
Houthi forces have advanced and captured strategic locations along Yemen's Red Sea coast.
The events come amid concerns over control of shipping routes like Bab al-Mandab.

positions.claim: Drones reportedly launched from Iraq struck the pipeline, according to US officials cited by CNN.
Saudi Arabia stated the attack originated in Iraq.

contested.point: Whether the pipeline attack and the Houthi advance are linked

positions.claim: Presents both as directly related events opening 'a new front in the Iran war'.
Reports both but frames the pipeline attack as blamed on Iraq, with Houthi advances part of the ongoing Yemen conflict — no direct operational link stated.

framing.note: Frames the events as a direct escalation — a 'new front' in a broader Iran war.
Emphasises the strategic jolt for Saudi Arabia from drones allegedly launched from Iraq.
Highlights the humanitarian crisis in Yemen and the struggle over strategic shipping routes.

jargon.plain: Saudi Arabia's main pipeline, moving crude from eastern oil fields to Red Sea export terminals — bypassing the Strait of Hormuz.
The narrow strait between Yemen and Djibouti linking the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden. A huge share of world shipping passes through it.
An Iran-backed Yemeni armed group, also called Ansar Allah, fighting Yemen's internationally recognised government.

stories.headline: Trump links the Iran war to oil prices and the midterms in a run of remarks

agreed_facts.text: US President Donald Trump made statements regarding the ongoing US-Iran war.
He claimed oil prices would fall as a result of US action.
He tied the conflict's outcome to the coming midterm elections.

contested.point: Whether oil prices will actually fall

positions.claim: Analysts quoted say supply risk in the Gulf keeps a floor under crude prices.
Reports the claim largely as stated, noting prices have eased from last week's spike.

contested.point: How central the midterms are to the strategy

positions.claim: Treats the electoral framing as the main story.
Leads on the military escalation and treats the election line as an aside.

framing.note: Market-first: what the remarks do to crude and to the rupee.
Politics-first: the remarks as a campaign message.
Conflict-first: the war timeline, with the comments as context.

jargon.plain: US elections held halfway through a presidential term. They decide control of Congress.
Unrefined oil. Its global price feeds straight into what you pay at the pump.

people.name: Donald Trump
people.who: President of the United States, making the statements in question.

stories.headline: Apple unveils a foldable iPhone duo as the price debate takes over the launch

agreed_facts.text: Apple announced two foldable iPhone models at its September event.
Indian pricing was announced above the outgoing Pro line.
Pre-orders open this week, with deliveries later this month.

positions.claim: Calls the hinge and display engineering a genuine generational jump.
Frames the pricing as out of step with Indian buying power and EMI budgets.
Positions it as a halo product to lift average selling prices.
Reports strong early interest from students on exchange offers.

framing.note: Product review lens — hardware first, price second.
Consumer-wallet lens — affordability and EMI maths.
Investor lens — margins and average selling price.

jargon.plain: The typical amount a company gets per device sold. Pricier models push it up.
Trading in your old phone for a discount on the new one.

stories.headline: Reports of Indian-origin suspects in overseas cases spark a coverage dispute

agreed_facts.text: Several overseas criminal cases this week involved suspects described as Indian-origin.
Officials in two of the countries involved confirmed arrests but not nationality details.
Indian diaspora groups asked outlets to stop leading with nationality.

contested.point: Whether nationality belongs in the headline

positions.claim: Keeps 'Indian-origin' in the headline as a matter of reader relevance.
Argues naming nationality without official confirmation risks collective blame.

contested.point: How many cases are actually connected

positions.claim: Reports the cases separately, with no link established.
Groups them as a pattern in a single round-up.

framing.note: Diaspora-interest lens — what it means for Indians abroad.
Media-ethics lens — the reporting itself is the story.
Wire lens — confirmed facts only, case by case.

jargon.plain: People from one country living permanently in others — here, Indians abroad.
Treating a whole group as responsible for what a few individuals did.
